name: tequila_guide
description: How to do a job in Tequila: one page of the guide, short enough to read whole, with tested examples. READ THE PAGE for an area before working in it for the first time. Topics: start (how to work here: look, change, check the picture, undo), materials (the library, changing a preset, types, colours), recipes (a material of your own), graph (the material graph and its nodes), textures (picture maps, texture packs, Substance), labels (logos and decals), uv (UV layouts), scene (parts, groups, moving, shapes, units, cutaways), lighting (environment, lights, floor), camera (views, lens, depth of field, composition), variants (colourways, Snapshots, configurator, studio presets), rendering (quick look, final render, queue, format, transparency, layers), image (the look after the render), animation (turntable, spin), fixing (a model that came in wrong), files (import, update, save, export), plugins, app (panels and preferences), scripting (raw requests, Python), shots (whole shots step by step). With no topic, the list of pages.

name: tequila_read
description: Read one part of the project, small enough to read: what is render (the render settings), image_style, color_management, environment (with its light pins and the floor), lighting, cameras, units, multi_materials (colourways), model_sets, studios (Snapshots), configurator, animation, product_turn, material_templates, measurements or textures - each as the command that sets it takes it back. index takes one entry of a list (one camera, one Snapshot). node reads one node of the scene by its id: its transform (place, turn and size), and a light's or a cutaway's settings. With nothing, what there is to read. Use it before any command that takes a whole block (render.set_settings, image.set_style, camera.set, studio.set, scene.set_light): read, change what was asked, send all of it back.

index.description: One entry of a part that is a list, numbered from 0.

node.description: A node's id, from tequila_nodes: read that node instead of a part.

name: tequila_scene
description: Counts, units, overall bounds and the file of the open scene.

name: tequila_nodes
description: Parts and groups: id, name, material and world size. Filter by a word in the name or material name to keep the answer short.

filter.description: Only nodes whose name or material name contains this (case-insensitive).

name: tequila_materials
description: Every material in the scene, briefly: id, name, type, how many parts use it and how many texture maps it has. tequila_material gives one in full.

name: tequila_material
description: One material of the scene in full: every parameter, pattern and texture map.

id.description: The material's id, from tequila_materials or tequila_nodes.

name: tequila_library
description: Search the material library: several hundred finished presets. LOOK HERE FIRST for any material, before making one. With no arguments it lists the categories and how many presets each has. search takes words that must all match the name, category, type, tags or description ("black leather", "brushed aluminium", "translucent ripstop"); category narrows to one. Answers with name, category, type and a line about each: the name is what tequila_library_apply takes.

search.description: Words to look for: a colour, a finish, what it is made of.

category.description: One category, as the list with no arguments names them.

limit.description: How many presets to answer with at most (default 20).

name: tequila_library_apply
description: Put a library preset on parts, by its exact name from tequila_library. One undo step. Answers with the material's id. color applies it in another colour: the same leather, wood or plastic with its pattern and finish kept, as a material of its own named for the colour ("Leather Tan #1f4d2b"). unlink=true gives the parts a copy of their own, to change without changing the other parts that use the preset. To change a preset's colour once it is on a part, use tequila_material_tint, not base_color: many presets keep their colour inside a pattern.

nodes.description: Part ids to put it on; the selection when left out.

color.description: A hex sRGB colour, e.g. "#1f4d2b", to apply the preset in.

name: tequila_command
description: How to write one command for tequila_apply: its exact fields and a working example, and for a setting-by-name command the names it takes. With no command, the name of every command. Ask before using a command for the first time, rather than guessing its fields.

name: tequila_add_shape
description: Add a simple shape as a new part: plane, cube, cylinder, sphere, disc, backdrop or wall. It stands beside what is in the scene, on the floor, half its size unless sizes are given. Not for the floor or the background, which the scene already has: those are settings of the environment (tequila_guide lighting). Sizes are metres: width (a cylinder's, sphere's and disc's diameter), depth, height, radius (half a round shape's width; a backdrop's curve). One undo step. Answers with the new part's id and its sizes.

name: tequila_query
description: A read-only query. Short answers: scene, selection, camera, commands, ui, jobs, history. Long ones, tens of thousands of characters on a real scene, which the tool named does a page at a time: context (tequila_read), api (tequila_command; the materials page of tequila_guide), materials (tequila_materials, tequila_material), nodes (tequila_nodes), library (tequila_library).

name: tequila_apply
description: Apply one command, as the guide's page for the job shows it (tequila_guide first), e.g. {"command":"material.set_type","material":2,"type":"velvet"}. tequila_command gives any command's exact fields and an example: ask it first. tequila_query what=api describes material parameters and types. One undo step. Colours may be hex sRGB strings ("value": "#c0392b"), converted for you; arrays are linear ACEScg.

name: tequila_material_guide
description: How to make procedural materials, a part at a time. With no topic: how to work, and the patterns and examples there are. topic recipe: the recipe format, the rules of thumb and the parameters that matter - read it before writing a first recipe. types: every material type; a type's id (plastic, metal, velvet...): the parameters it shows. patterns: every pattern in a line; a pattern's kind (leather, weave, wood_advanced...): its settings and defaults. examples: the 16 tested recipes in a line each; an example's name (Terrazzo, Walnut, Carbon Fibre...): its recipe, to change and preview.

topic.description: contents, recipe, types, patterns, examples, a type's id, a pattern's kind or an example's name.

name: tequila_material_preview
description: Show a material recipe (or an existing material by id) on a ball, without changing the scene. Returns an image. The fastest way to try an idea: preview, adjust, preview again, then tequila_material_create. Recipe: {"name": "Speckled Stone", "type": "plastic" (or metal, glass, paint, velvet... see the guide), any parameter as a value ("specular_roughness": 0.3, "base_color": "#c0392b" - hex sRGB is fine), "patterns": [{"param": "base_color", "procedural": {"kind": "noise"}, "size": 0.01, "colors": [{"at": 0, "color": "#d8d4cc"}, {"at": 1, "color": "#a9a59c"}]}, {"param": "specular_roughness", "procedural": {"kind": "noise"}, "size": 0.02, "range": [0.2, 0.4]}, {"param": "bump", "procedural": {"kind": "leather"}, "size": 0.002, "depth": 0.0001}]}. `size` is the feature size in metres at real-world scale. A later pattern on the same param is a layer: "blend" mix/multiply/add, "amount" 0-1, "mask" {"threshold": 0.5, "softness": 0.05}. Pattern kinds: noise, noise_texture, ridged, cellular, spots, granite, marble, wood, wood_advanced, brushed, brushed_radial, scratches, leather, weave, camouflage, contour, mesh. Call tequila_material_guide once for what each looks like, their settings, the rules of thumb and 16 tested example recipes to start from.

radius.description: The ball's radius in metres (default 0.025). Use the real part's size to judge pattern scale.

name: tequila_material_create
description: Make a new material from a recipe and put it on parts, as one undo step. Only when tequila_library has nothing close: search it first. Returns its id and a preview image. Recipe: {"name": "Speckled Stone", "type": "plastic" (or metal, glass, paint, velvet... see the guide), any parameter as a value ("specular_roughness": 0.3, "base_color": "#c0392b" - hex sRGB is fine), "patterns": [{"param": "base_color", "procedural": {"kind": "noise"}, "size": 0.01, "colors": [{"at": 0, "color": "#d8d4cc"}, {"at": 1, "color": "#a9a59c"}]}, {"param": "specular_roughness", "procedural": {"kind": "noise"}, "size": 0.02, "range": [0.2, 0.4]}, {"param": "bump", "procedural": {"kind": "leather"}, "size": 0.002, "depth": 0.0001}]}. `size` is the feature size in metres at real-world scale. A later pattern on the same param is a layer: "blend" mix/multiply/add, "amount" 0-1, "mask" {"threshold": 0.5, "softness": 0.05}. Pattern kinds: noise, noise_texture, ridged, cellular, spots, granite, marble, wood, wood_advanced, brushed, brushed_radial, scratches, leather, weave, camouflage, contour, mesh. Call tequila_material_guide once for what each looks like, their settings, the rules of thumb and 16 tested example recipes to start from.

nodes.description: Part ids to put it on; the selection when left out.

preview.description: Return a preview image too (default true).

name: tequila_material_update
description: Remake an existing material from a recipe, where it is: every part using it changes. One undo step; returns a preview image. Use it to refine a material after looking at it on the product. Recipe: {"name": "Speckled Stone", "type": "plastic" (or metal, glass, paint, velvet... see the guide), any parameter as a value ("specular_roughness": 0.3, "base_color": "#c0392b" - hex sRGB is fine), "patterns": [{"param": "base_color", "procedural": {"kind": "noise"}, "size": 0.01, "colors": [{"at": 0, "color": "#d8d4cc"}, {"at": 1, "color": "#a9a59c"}]}, {"param": "specular_roughness", "procedural": {"kind": "noise"}, "size": 0.02, "range": [0.2, 0.4]}, {"param": "bump", "procedural": {"kind": "leather"}, "size": 0.002, "depth": 0.0001}]}. `size` is the feature size in metres at real-world scale. A later pattern on the same param is a layer: "blend" mix/multiply/add, "amount" 0-1, "mask" {"threshold": 0.5, "softness": 0.05}. Pattern kinds: noise, noise_texture, ridged, cellular, spots, granite, marble, wood, wood_advanced, brushed, brushed_radial, scratches, leather, weave, camouflage, contour, mesh. Call tequila_material_guide once for what each looks like, their settings, the rules of thumb and 16 tested example recipes to start from.

recipe.description: The new recipe. Without a name the material keeps its own.

preview.description: Return a preview image too (default true).

name: tequila_material_tint
description: Make a material the same material in another colour, wherever its colour is kept: a plain value, the colours inside a pattern, the stops of a ramp. THE way to recolour a library preset ("make this leather dark green", "that denim in red"): its pattern, grain, weave and finish stay, the colour asked for becomes its main colour, and its other colours keep their relation to it - creases stay darker, pale threads paler - while colours of another family (white threads, rust on steel) are left alone. Every part using the material changes; material.unlink a part first to change it alone. One undo step. Answers with the colour it was, each parameter changed and how many colours, and a preview image. Refuses a material with no colour of its own (its colour is a picture, or a thin film's) and says why.

material.description: The material's id, from tequila_nodes, tequila_materials or tequila_library_apply.

preview.description: Return a preview image too (default true).

name: tequila_material_recipe
description: Read any material - one you made, or a library preset already on a part - back as a recipe, to change it and send it to tequila_material_update or tequila_material_create.

name: tequila_material_save
description: Keep a material in the person's own material library, so it is in the Library tab for every project.

name: tequila_batch
description: Several operations as ONE undo step. Each is a request object with an "op": apply, select, frame, look, ui, import, save, screenshot, queue. If one fails the whole batch is taken back, unless atomic is false.

name: tequila_undo
description: Take back the last step (a single edit or a whole batch).

name: tequila_redo
description: Put back the last undone step.

name: tequila_select
description: Replace the selection with these node ids.

name: tequila_frame
description: Point the camera at everything, or at the selection. This moves the view the person is looking at: for when they ask for one, or to find something out of sight - not after a material edit, which leaves the camera where it was.

all.description: true for everything (default), false for the selection.

name: tequila_look
description: Place the camera: a standard view, orbit angles around a target, or an exact eye position. Undoable. The view is the person's too: read it first (tequila_query camera) if you mean to put it back.

from.description: Eye position [x, y, z]; not with yaw/pitch/distance.

yaw.description: Degrees around +Y; 0 looks from the front.

name: tequila_screenshot
description: See the application as it is now. Returns an image. After a change the rendered view is dark and grainy for a few seconds while it redraws: this waits for the picture to finish, up to settle seconds, and says with the image whether it had. Do not judge a look from one it calls unfinished: look again.

viewport.description: true for just the 3D view, without panels (default true).

settle.description: Seconds to give the picture to finish (default 12; 0 takes it at once).

window.description: One of Tequila's other windows instead, which must be open: uv (the UV editor), graph (the Material Graph editor), render (the Render window), preferences.

name: tequila_render
description: Render the current view to an image and return it. Blocks Tequila while it runs: keep it small (e.g. 640x400, 32 samples). wireframe=true draws the model's edges instead, as the project's Wireframe settings say - no ray tracing, a second or two at any size.

name: tequila_queue
description: Start a background render with the document's render settings; returns a job id at once. Poll tequila_jobs. studio renders one view; studios=true renders every view; configurations=true every valid combination of the configurator; frames=true the frames of the turntable (animation.set), one render each, leaving out those already rendered.

studio.description: A Studio (a view) by name or index, applied for the render and taken back.

studios.description: Every Studio, one render each, named for its view.

engine.description: The engine for this render; the document's when left out.

configurations.description: One render for every valid combination of the configurator, named by its choices.

frames.description: One render for every frame of the turntable, the product turned to each frame's angle; the file name takes the frame's number.

first.description: With frames: the first frame to render (default 0).

last.description: With frames: the last frame to render (default the last there is).

name: tequila_jobs
description: The background render queue: state, progress and output file of each job.

name: tequila_studio_presets
description: The studio presets installed: complete studios - lights, cameras and views, floor, look - for a kind of product, by family and size. Each lists its views and the product radius it was framed for; "suggested" marks the size in each family nearest the product in the scene.

name: tequila_studio_preset_apply
description: Apply an installed studio preset as ONE undo step: its lights, cameras and views (Studios), environment and floor, look and render settings, framed to the product's size and the product stood on its floor. The first view is applied; tequila_studio_render_all renders them all.

front.description: The product's side that should face the Main camera (default +z).

scale.description: What follows the product's size (default: the preset's own choice).

keep_placement.description: Leave the product where it is.

dress.description: Also put the preset's materials on parts by their names (its material rules).

name: tequila_studio_preset_save
description: Keep the scene's studio - everything but the product - as a studio preset of the person's own, framed for the product it has now.

materials.description: Keep the project's materials with it.

name: tequila_studio_render_all
description: Render every view (Studio) in the background, one image each, named for its view. Only when asked for renders.

name: tequila_stop
description: Stop the running background render; it still writes its image, and the jobs waiting behind it start. job stops one job by its id from tequila_jobs: the one rendering is stopped, one still waiting is taken out of the queue and writes nothing. all=true stops the one rendering and takes out every job waiting: how to end a spin, a turntable or a batch of views early.

name: tequila_ui
description: Open or close panels and switch the viewport shading.

frame.description: Show the viewport at the render's size and shape (on by default).

selection_outline.description: The selection's outline in the viewport (Shift+H); hiding it keeps the selection.

gizmo.description: The move, turn and scale gizmo on the selection (Shift+G).

start_screen.description: The start screen, with recent projects and the sample scenes.

updates.description: Help > Check for updates. Opening it asks GitHub for the latest release.

graph.description: Open the Material Graph editor on this material number; false closes it.

name: tequila_preferences
description: Tequila's own settings, as Edit > Preferences shows them, a page at a time. With no arguments, the pages there are. page is one of general, interface, viewport, navigation, keyboard (the shortcuts), import, folders, updates: each of its settings with its key, value, default and what it takes. search finds settings by words in their name or help. set and reset answer with what changed. They are the person's own and kept between sessions: change one only when asked to.

search.description: Words that must all be in a setting's key, label or help: "zoom", "autosave".

set.description: Settings to change, by name: {"viewport.gizmo_size": 150, "navigation.invert_zoom": true}. All are checked before any is taken. A keyboard shortcut is set the same way: {"shortcut.view.screenshot": "F12"}, a list of two keys, or "" for none.

reset.description: "all", a page (general, interface, viewport, navigation, keyboard, import, folders, updates), a setting, a shortcut, or a list of settings, put back to their defaults.

name: tequila_import
description: Load a model file into the scene: STEP or IGES (CAD, divided into parts with their colours), Rhino .3dm (layers, materials, blocks), Blender .blend (read by the Blender installed here, materials node for node), glTF/GLB, FBX, OBJ, STL, 3MF, PLY, USD (.usda, .usdc or .usdz) or IFC.

up.description: Which way up the file was drawn: z for a CAD model drawn Z up, which otherwise comes in lying on its back. Without it, the setting File > Up axis of imports decides.

lighting.description: For a Blender file with lights of its own: blender lights the model with them, its world and its exposure, as it looks in Blender; tequila keeps the scene's lighting; ask asks the person in Tequila's window. Without it, the setting File > Lights in Blender files decides.

name: tequila_save
description: Save the project, to its own file or to a new path.

name: tequila_graph_nodes
description: The catalogue of nodes a material graph can hold: what each is for, with its inputs, outputs, settings and fields. With nothing, the first page of them all, a line each, and the families. search takes words that must all match ("voronoi", "edge wear", "brushed"); family narrows to one (input, texture, pattern, group, color, converter, vector, shader, simple, layout). Three or fewer answers come whole; name asks for one whole. LOOK A NODE UP HERE before adding it: never guess a node's name, an input or a setting.

name.description: One node whole, by its name in the catalogue: voronoi_texture, gradient, pattern_leather, knurl.

page.description: Which page of a long list, from 1.

name: tequila_graph_read
description: A material's node graph in brief: each node on a line with its id, what it is and where its output goes, and which of the material's parameters the graph drives. With node, that one node whole: its settings and fields, each input with its value or the wire into it, each output with where it goes. A few hundred characters where the whole material (tequila_material) is thousands.

material.description: The material's id, from tequila_materials or tequila_nodes.

node.description: A node's id from the brief reading, or "surface".

page.description: Which page of a graph with many nodes, from 1.

name: tequila_graph_edit
description: Change a material's node graph one step at a time, each one undo step; a graph that would not work is refused and nothing changes. action is: add (node: a name from tequila_graph_nodes; settings, fields, inputs and label may come with it) - answers with the new node's id and its sockets; set (node: an id; settings {key: value}, fields {the node's own fields, such as a bump's depth or a ramp's gradient}, inputs {an input's name: a number, "#rrggbb", [x, y, z] or null for its default}, label, muted); connect (from: a node id, output: its name when the node has several, to: a node id or left out for the surface, input: the input's name, or on the surface a parameter's key such as base_color, specular_roughness, bump); disconnect (node: an id or left out for the surface, input); remove (node: an id). Every part that wears the material changes: material.unlink a part first to change it alone. Look with tequila_material_preview.

node.description: add: the name of the node to add. set, remove, disconnect: the id of a node in the graph, or "surface".

settings.description: A general node's settings by key: {"feature": "f2"}.

fields.description: The node's own fields, as tequila_graph_read shows them: {"depth": 0.0003}, {"gradient": [{"at": 0, "color": "#101010"}, {"at": 1, "color": "#d0d0d0"}]}, {"procedural": {"frequency": 900}}, {"value": 0.35}.

inputs.description: Values for inputs nothing is wired into, by the input's name: {"Scale": 40, "Color1": "#202020"}.

from.description: connect: the node the wire leaves.

output.description: connect: which output of it, by name; the first when left out.

to.description: connect: the node the wire goes into; the surface when left out.

input.description: connect, disconnect: the input by its name, or a parameter's key on the surface.

name: tequila_uv_islands
description: A part's UV layout, island by island, largest first: each island's number (what the uv.* commands take), its box on the layout, how much of the part it is, its area, how stretched it is, and where on the part it lies - centre and size in the world's metres and the way it faces. How to tell which island is the front panel before moving, packing, cutting or stitching one. Numbers change after a cut or an unwrap: read again.

page.description: Which page of a layout with many islands, from 1.

name: tequila_uv_cut
description: Cut a seam in a part's UV layout where you mean it, as one undo step. path is two or more points ON THE PART, each [x, y, z] in the world's metres (tequila_nodes gives the part's centre and size; tequila_uv_islands each island's): the cut follows the part's own edges the shortest way from each point to the next - down the back of a bottle is [[0, top, -r], [0, bottom, -r]]. A seam follows the mesh's edges: across a flat CAD face that has none it is refused, and says the way round. Or sharper_than: every edge inside an island that is sharper than that many degrees (islands narrows it to some). The pieces are laid flat again in place; pack=true also packs the whole layout after. Answers with how many islands there were and are.

path.description: Points on the part, in the world's metres.

sharper_than.description: Degrees: cut every edge inside an island that is sharper than this.

islands.description: With sharper_than: only inside these islands.

pack.description: Pack the whole layout into the square afterwards.

reflatten.description: Lay the pieces the cut touches flat again (default true).

across.description: With path: carry a cut that stops just short of the island's edge on to it, so it divides the island (default true). false cuts between the points exactly, for a slit.

name: tequila_uv_stitch
description: Join islands of a part's UV layout along the seams between them, as one undo step: two or more islands that meet on the part, by their numbers from tequila_uv_islands, or one island to shut a seam inside it. The smaller is moved onto the larger. Islands that do not touch on the part are refused.

name: tequila_improve
description: Improve model, for a model that came in coarse: the parts at and under a node made finer or shaded again, as one undo step. subdivide (1 to 3) makes four triangles of every one each time, the new points following the curve of the surface, for curves that show their facets; shade (degrees, 30 is usual) works the shading out again, smooth across edges gentler than that, for an STL or OBJ that looks faceted all over. With neither, how many triangles there are and how many each would make. A CAD model (STEP, IGES) is better divided again from its exact surfaces: page fixing of tequila_guide.

node.description: A part, or a group: everything under it.

shade.description: Degrees, 5 to 90: edges sharper than this stay sharp.

crease.description: With subdivide, for a mesh that had no shading: edges sharper than this stay sharp (default 30).

name: tequila_model_units
description: Units of this model: put right a model that came in the wrong size because its file named no unit (an STL in millimetres is read as metres, a thousand times too large). unit is what its numbers really are: mm, cm, in, ft or m. The whole model the node belongs to is scaled about the middle of its base, so it stands where it stood; one undo step. With no unit, its size now and the size it would be in each unit: pick the one that reads as the real thing. read_as says what its numbers are read as now, when not metres.

name: tequila_plugin_guide
description: How to write a Tequila plugin: the full reference (manifest, Python API, panels and their field types, events, material packs), a working template, and the way to work - write, ask the person to turn it on, run, read the log, fix. Read it once before writing a plugin.

name: tequila_plugin_list
description: Every installed plugin: id, name, version, whether it is on, running or failed (and why), its commands, panels and events, and its folder. Also whether Python was found, and the person's plugins folder.

name: tequila_plugin_write
description: Write a plugin's files into the person's plugins folder: a new plugin, or new versions of an existing one's files (others are kept). Give plugin.json (its id must be `id`) and main.py at least for a new one. Text files only (.py .json .md .txt .csv .toml .ini .cfg), paths inside the plugin's folder. A running plugin restarts with the new code; a new one must be turned on with tequila_plugin_enable.

id.description: The plugin id and folder name, e.g. "my.batch-renamer": letters, digits, . - _

files.description: Path inside the plugin folder -> the file's full text, e.g. {"plugin.json": "...", "main.py": "..."}.

name: tequila_plugin_enable
description: Turn a plugin on. A plugin with Python code runs as the person, so Tequila asks them in its Plugins window and only they can say yes: tell them to look at Tequila, then check tequila_plugin_list for "enabled". A material pack is turned on at once.

name: tequila_plugin_run
description: Run one of an enabled plugin's commands (or a panel button's command) with `values` as its panel would send them, wait a little, and return what it logged: its prints, status messages, `finished`, or the traceback if it failed. A command with a panel opens the panel instead.

values.description: Field id -> value, as the panel would send.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for it to finish (default 10, at most 120).

name: tequila_plugin_log
description: The last lines of a plugin's log: what it printed, its status messages, finished commands and tracebacks. Use it to debug.

name: tequila_request
description: Send any raw request object (with an "op") for anything the other tools do not cover.
